**Finding: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)**

The problem sits in Section 7.0 (Materials), reached via the disclaimers section:

- **Default ownership runs the wrong way.** p0082: "If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials." Type II Materials are those in which "IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)" (p0085). So every bespoke deliverable IBM produces for us defaults to IBM ownership.
- **The licence back is too narrow to save it.** The Type II licence is irrevocable, worldwide and paid-up, but only "within Customer's Enterprise only", with no right to prepare derivative works and no sublicensing — so it misses the fallback (use, modify **and** sublicense for our business). "Enterprise" is also cut down to US-located entities (p0021).
- **No Customer Data/Content ownership statement.** § 11.6 only makes us responsible for Content, § 14.18 covers contact data, and § 14.17 grants no implied rights — but nothing affirms our ownership of Content and Customer Components.

IBM's ownership of its Base Components/platform (§ 12.1) is fine and untouched. IBM's broad non-exclusive licence back over Type I Materials (p0084) is noted but not flagged, as it does not disturb our ownership.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** flip the default so Materials created during the Service performance period are Type I (Customer-owned), leaving IBM's pre-existing works as Type II; and add a new Section 7(e) confirming we retain all right, title and interest in Content and Customer Components. The comment offers IBM the fallback of keeping the Type II default if we get a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense.
